headline: Scentre Group CEO Elliott Rusanow outlines retail sales growth, housing pipeline, JV capital recycling and redevelopment strategy as core earnings drivers.
reasoning: Retail sales at Scentre's destinations grew over 5.2% in the first half of the year, driven by more foot traffic and increased demand for space from business partners. The group holds 670 hectares of strategically located land with potential for 25,000 homes, which Rusanow sees as a long-term earnings contributor via the 'going up' (vertical housing) opportunity leveraging existing transport, energy and infrastructure. The joint venture program — which has raised $3.1 billion through 50% stake sales including the recent Westfield Mount Gravatt deal with Australian Retirement Trust — was a deliberate post-pandemic funding strategy that avoided equity dilution. Future JV partnerships will be opportunistic rather than structural. Redevelopment spend includes a $240 million Westfield Bondi Junction makeover plus works at Penrith, Tuggerah, Parramatta and Bourgoin in Perth, all aimed at capturing experiential spending and growing earnings per security.
quote: Retail sales of our business partners grew by in excess of 5.2% in the first six months of this year. The sales continue to grow. They grow because more people are coming and the demand for space from businesses to come and take space with us and partner with us to interact with our customer is seeing our sales that are generated within our destinations continue to grow, and our shareholder receive increasing earnings per security. Now you're sitting on more than 670 hectares of strategically located land. We mentioned a potential pipeline here of more than 25,000 homes. This is what Australia needs. We have a housing shortage.
episode_title: Scentre’s property play goes beyond the shopping centre

headline: Scentre Group sees Australia's housing shortage as a long-term opportunity to develop up to 25,000 homes on its existing 670 hectares of urban land.
reasoning: Australia and New Zealand face significant housing supply constraints. Scentre's portfolio of 670 hectares of land in established urban locations — already connected to energy, transport infrastructure and millions of weekly visitors — positions it to contribute to housing supply through vertical (going up) development rather than greenfield expansion. This is characterised as a very long-term earnings opportunity, with no near-term financial guidance provided.
quote: We see a very long term opportunity to be part of the housing supply solution that this country needs. We, as you said, 670 hectares of land, some of which is occupied by our destinations, but it's already in in-built urban locations that has the opportunity to be identified, to have more activity occur. Part of the housing supply will be delivered by going up, not just going out. We are part of the going up proposition and going up makes a lot of sense. Energy is already connected to our sites. Transport infrastructure is co-located with our sites. Thousands of people are employed in our destinations, and millions of people come there each and every week.
episode_title: Scentre’s property play goes beyond the shopping centre
